comment: Very irresponsible person, the class has no serious academic inside it besides just chatting about "situational" and "ambiguous". Grading is too arbitrary and random, based on luck of getting called and at the correct time. Group projects grading is even more strange. Classroom rules are never enforced, those who use cell phones worked out fine.

Dr. Cruz's class helped me become a better thinker. The class was very well organized and case analyses added a lot of value to the material. You need to participate every class and come prepared, but you will gain a lot from it if you do. This class is for someone who likes a challenge and likes to be pushed outside of his/her comfort zone.

Great professor. Hard grader for presentations but fully possible to get a good grade if you put in the work. Do not take this if you want to take the easy way out. It is a great class that will teach a lot but you need to be willing to put in effort.

Best teacher I had this year by far. Participation is 40% of the grade, so it really makes you pay attention and get involved in the discussion. Not an easy class, but extremely interesting if you do the work. Makes you a better speaker and critical thinker.

In terms of the strengths of Dr. Cruz, I might not have enough space available to note all of them. Dr. Cruz inspires his students to learn the material, and his discussion-based style allows his students to work on their argumentative and analytical skills. You will miss out on an incredible opportunity if you do not take his OB course.

This was the second class I have taken with Dr. Cruz. Compared to his OB class, Groups and Teams is far more casual. Presentations are less formal, and students have the opportunity to be really creative with their projects. Dr. Cruz is a fun professor and every class is new and exciting.
This professor is very interested in the subject and will get you engaged in the course. This was just a very easy subject to learn.

This is my second course with Professor Cruz, and he is easily the best professor I have taken in the business school. If every teacher were as fair, engaged, and excited to teach as he was, the business school would be a far better place. So long as you prepare for class and engage, you will have a rewarding experience. The absolute man.

Really interesting class! Based solely around a semester long team competition. Prof. Cruz is animated and excited to teach the subject. The material is manageable and the assignments are interesting such as a presentation on a local business etc.

Managing Groups and Teams is a really fun and engaging class. Professor Cruz does a great job of facilitating class discussion and gets the class thinking critically. Overall a really great class to take for a management elective. He has a clear grading rubric and lays out everything you need to know to be successful.

Professor Cruz is far and away the best professor I've had at the Robins school of business and at UR. He has clear grading criteria and engaging classwork. He is skilled at running a classroom conversation, and empowers students to advocate for their ideas while always being respectful. Come to class, do the readings, get a good grade.

Professor Cruz is a good guy. He can be intimidating because he's a big believer in the Socratic method. He'll pretty much ask you "why?" on anything you say to see if you're BSing or actually stand behind what you mean. Fun class. The class is made up of all group activities that are actually really fun. Take this class if you have a free class!

Professor Cruz is a great professor. Will make you show constant effort to participate otherwise your grade will not be great. Very accessible and responds to emails quickly and offers (at least for my semester) and single opportunity for extra credit. Grading is heavily weighted in participation and presentations but the final is a takehome paper

If youre trying to take OB and you value class participation and presentations, Cruz is the man. He stimulates discussion and every class turns into a back and forth debate. No tests in this class. Take Cruz. Hes a savage.

if you don't like participating or group projects, don't take this class. He's a tough grader for cases, and participation is 40% of your grade. However, he is an amazing professor and is very good at stimulating student interest.
You gotta show up, its imperative. Outside of showing up, if you read the cases and have some questions prepared for every class, you will do well. Good guy, good class, fun times.
40% of grade is participation so take OB with someone else if you tend not to participate

Cruz can definitely come off as intimidating at the beginning of the semester but don't let that scare you off. The class is entirely discussion and presentation based, so as long as you are willing to participate you'll do fine. Highly recommend, definitely best prof for OB

Professor Cruz pushes students to really think about what they say. The class is easy if you pay attention and participate well (don't just talk to talk). Sometimes Professor Cruz can say things that are mean so you have to have thick skin to take this class. There is a lot of teamwork that is involved as well.

Before taking this class, I heard that Professor Cruz was very intimidating and that the class was extremely difficult. While the class did end up being very challenging, it was in a way that helped improve my learning. I was a bit intimidated at first, but it was just him trying to challenge us to learn in a more effective way than other classes.

Professor Cruz is hands down one of the best professors I have ever had. You need to have thick skin and you need to participate. Once you have those two things down, you will learn so much from him. Take this class if you want to learn. Course work is not terrible. Cases are enjoyable, barely read the textbook, and he's not a harsh grader.

If you're soft, don't take him. Good teacher who makes students think critically. If you're only a bschool major you're probably not used to the way he runs his classes but they're very discussion based and he really pushes you on arguments. Don't really need to read the book or prepare and can still get an A in participation which is like 30%

Cruz comes off as and has a reputation for being strict and intimidating, but he really isn't. He is tough and critical but only to help you improve. He has helped me improve my critical thinking and public speaking immensely. The class does not teach practical skills. The class is majority discussion. Cruz is a good guy, and is not a bad choice.

Professor Cruz is easily the best Organizational Behavior professor at Richmond. While the beginning of the class may seem intimidating and a lot of students will end up dropping the class, you will learn as you move through the semester that sticking in the class will be one of the best decisions you've made.

Dr. Cruz is one of the best professors I've ever had. He pushes people to think very critically and analytically Anybody who doesn't like him is extremely sensitive and can't handle being pushed outside of their comfort zone. I would recommend him to anyone who is taking this course to actually get something out of it.

Dr Cruz is a tough professor, and you will have to work hard to get the grades. Participation is incredibly important. He is a fair grader but sometimes hard to know what he wants in terms of content. Pretty pedantic so make sure you have a high attention to detail. Wants his students to do well, but you have to put in the work
Professor Cruz is very engaging. He creates an environment where participation is encouraged.

People will tell you not to take him because he is very intimidating on the first day of class. Give it a week or two and you'll be glad you stayed. The thing with OB is that a lot of professors will make it lecture and theory heavy, and this class is purely discussion based and is a lot of fun.
First class he seems brutal but it gets better with time. If you don't participate in class, don't take the course. Tough grader but he has clear rubrics that allow you to do well if you try.

Dr. Cruz is a great professor and really encourages his students to think critically and creatively. Class is often structured like a debate and can get intense. This makes the class extremely entertaining and enjoyable to attend.

Professor Cruz is the most engaging professor I've had at Robins School of Business. His course is challenging and interesting without being too difficult. Cruz fosters an environment in class where students feel empowered to share their opinions and know that what they say will be respected. I look forward to this class every day.

Professor Cruz comes off as very strict and scary but once the class starts rolling, he becomes fun. He expects a lot of you and makes you work hard during your assignments. He prepares you more for the real world more than another class and makes you think critically about everything.

Dr. Cruz is a really great professor. He is super engaging and knows a lot about Groups & Teams. The class is very interactive and I look forward to attending class each day. This class is definitely something which you should take prior to graduating from RSB.

I had Dr. Cruz for an elective this year, and his enthusiasm for and knowledge of the material was awesome to be around. He expects a lot of his students, but gives them the tools to succeed. He also increased my ability to think both critically and analytically, while somehow keeping class fun.

Professor Cruz is a very good teacher but be ready for for some sarcasm and be ready to stand up to your beliefs/opinions. He will challenge what you will say with some of the research he has performed, but if you explain your opinion clearly he will respect it and encourage you for more. Participation is highly encouraged

Dr. Cruz is the man. He is funny (sarcastic), smart, and really cares about his class. This class very much experiential learning as you manage your own group or team. Fun challenges for a performance bonus at the end of the year. Grading is participation, 3 presentations, and a weekly journal. You must attend class and participate. Take this class

Dr. Cruz knows his content very well and can teach you a lot about a subject if you are willing to put in the work. Participation is very important in the class. If you enjoy voicing your opinion and being competitive, you will enjoy this class.

Dr. Cruz highly values class participation. If you don't participate, you likely won't do well in his class. Also, there are 3 presentations you have to give, and a simple take-home final. All of those things make up a majority of your grade. Cruz is a pretty funny and smart guy, but be ready to debate and speak up in class if you want an A
Class is engaging and fun to be in. Much tougher than other OB professors. 40% participation, three group presentations and a take-home final.

He is a great professor for OB. Some people chose not to take him because he is not the easiest choice and he knows that. However, if you enjoy debating with other classmates and calling each other out, then this is the perfect class. Each class is like a battle and it is very fun. It is like an academic brawl. Overall, he is a great professor!

There are not tests in this class, there are 3 cases assigned to your team (you select case and team at the beginning). The cases are presented to the rest of the class, he grades presentations harshly. The final exam is a written case study were you answer one question, you can work with as many people in the class as you want and submit 1 answer.
A lot of reading and heavily weighted on participation. So be ready for that.

Dr. Cruz can come off as a bit abrasive to some, but he has been one of my favorite professors here at UR. His class is almost entirely discussion based (40%) and often will devolve into a likely debate over the topics for the day. He doesn't tend to stress the material, but instead concentrates on your logic and critical thinking. 10/10

He tries to scare you on the first day by saying he is the hardest OB professor but the class is very good. Class is very driven by participation is 40% of your grade you have to be paying attention to your arguments in class or he will call you out on it. Case Analysis that are group projects which make up the rest of the grade

Dr. Cruz is a good teacher and definitely knows a lot about Organizational Behavior. Class participation is super important, if you don't participate you will not get a good grade and presentations are also graded hard. If you do the work definitely manageable to pull of an A and you will definitely learn a lot.

Professor Cruz is one of the best professors I've had here at Richmond. He is different, that is for sure, and sometimes harsh and can come off as stern. But that is just his personality. He is clear about guidelines and expects hard work from his students. You give him that and you will get a decent grade. Do all the case readings VERY CAREFULLY

Dr. Cruz challenges his students to think analytically, develop a strong speaking voice, and present professionally. While he is a tough greater, he is extremely diplomatic and responsive to feedback. This was one of the most intellectually stimulating classes I've ever taken at UR and I would recommend Dr. Cruz to anyone who loves a challenge.

Participation is one of the biggest components of this course (40% total grade). If you don't enjoy speaking in class or group presentations, it will be difficult to succeed in this class. Dr. Cruz will challenge your ideas in order to refine them, so I recommend being defensive without taking offense. Overall, this course was very manageable!

don't take his comments personal but rather as a hint for you to reflect upon your own belief system and knowledge. Dr. Cruz corresponds is a great professor. he does not give grades because he wants good evaluations but because if follow his criteria, you will have learned a lot! he is very willing to help if you ask for career advising.

I went into this class knowing relatively nothing about OB, and Cruz was really able to instill in me a genuine interest for the topic. My confidence in my opinions and the evidence to support them has grown in this class.  He might scare you the first day with his level of intensity, but it's completely worth it to stick around.

Heavy participation grade. Prepare for each class, and speak up. Understand the grading criteria for group assignments. You will learn and retain OB more from this class than other professors, but you will have to work harder and understand the expectations.

Professor Cruz challenges students in a way few professors do.  In many other classes, you can be intellectually lazy in discussions. Cruz, however, pushes you to clarify your points, to think critically, and to be clear and concise.  If you are someone who wants to become a better student while learning about OB, take his class.
Dr. Cruz is very tough the first week to scare away people who aren't committed. There are easier choices at Richmond for OB, but if you don't mind some extra effort Dr. Cruz is a great choice.

i loved this course. 40% of your grade is participation. He will challenge everything you say. Classes are purely discussion and presentation based so keep that in mind. It's not hard workload wise but that work has to be quality. Grading is pretty fair. I have enjoyed this class and would reccomend it to anyone who likes discussion based classes.

In my opinion Professor Cruz makes his class very interesting and engaging. It is clear that he really wants to hear what we have to say. He has no problem harshly questioning us if he does not think we are giving him enough in our answers, which you definitely need to get used to. He also grades pretty toughly, but overall I would recommend him.

Dr. Cruz is a hard grader. He expects nothing but the best and expects you to think critically. Be ready to talk in class. If you have a weak argument, he will argue and ask many questions so be ready to defend yourself. He likes to seem harder and tougher than he actually is. Be ready to work hard for your grade.

Dr. Cruz is a really good professor but he approaches the class as if the students are only taking his class and no other class at the same time. This puts a lot of extra stress on students who have already a strenuous class schedule.

Dr. Cruz has definite expectations of performance within his course, but don't let him scare you on the first day of class. He does not allow much leeway in participation or attendance, but it requires students to stay engaged in class. Make sure you pick a good group for your presentations because you keep the group all semester.

Participation is 40% of final grade, using a scale of 0, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100 every single class. There are 3 group presentations throughout the semester - choose your group and cases wisely on the first day. Prepare for each class thoroughly and speak a lot. However, make sure your comments are thoughtful because he will challenge you.

He treats you like an adult, requiring that you participate and support your ideas. If you don't like being pushed to justify your answers, drop the course. If you aren't ready to work hard, drop the course. If you want to learn and be engaged every day, this is the course for you.
Dr. Cruz is very intimidating at the beginning, but you soon pick up on his sense of humor. Participation is huge, so don't take if you don't like talking in class

Dr. Cruz is a 5 because of personal preference. He is not the easiest OB professor, however his class will 100% be the most rewarding. Lots of group work that is challenging, but worth it in the end. Realistically, you are rewarded for hard work, however you have to be willing to put time in

Dr. Cruz is an excellent choice if you enjoy seminar style classes and don't mind being challenged. He is a very tough grader and the case analysis presentations are difficult. Don't miss class. Also, he comes off rude to some students but if you challenge him right back and are blunt with your thoughts then he will respect you.

If you naturally talk a lot in class you'll be fine. But your comments have to be well thought out because he is not afraid to speak up and call you out on a weak argument. Annoying how he's obsessively meticulous with formatting and grading (won't round up an 89.9) but I thought it was good/unique experience overall. Get ready to talk!!!

You gotta do 3 presentations. Prepare well. I can't stress it enough, but really, prepare well. Challenges you. At the end of the semester, if you FINALLY realize that OB is important, you'll see how good your class was. Participation is really important. He has a bad reputation, but he's working at it. I really like him.

Professor Cruz is one of the best professors I've had at Richmond.  Class participation is a big part of the course, but leads to extremely interesting and useful discussions.  If you do all of your assignments on time and stay on top of the readings, you will be able to do well.
